title: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
excerpt: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models often exceed a single accelerator's memory capacity. Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path. We present Specter, an inference system that uses quantization to combine speculative decoding with expert offloading. Its lightweight quantized draft model runs efficiently on device while preserving high-fidelity expert activation patterns. This provides accurate multi-step lookahead over future expert usage, allowing the runtime to organize expert movement and execution ahead of verification and improve both communication and execution efficiency. Under…

ai.summary: Specter is an inference system that uses a quantized draft model for speculative decoding while offloading MoE experts, reducing PCIe bottlenecks.
ai.why: It enables faster, lower‑latency inference for large MoE models on limited hardware, useful for production deployments.

title: SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration
excerpt: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps. Feature caching reduces this cost by reusing features across denoising steps. Recent forecasting methods extend this idea by extrapolating features to skipped steps instead of reusing them. However, existing forecasting methods extrapolate the features they predict uniformly, even though the spatial-frequency components of these features change most at different stages of denoising. They also overlook that denoising progresses nonuniformly, so equal step intervals can correspond to very different…

ai.summary: The paper "SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration" proposes a Kalman‑filter‑based method to forecast transformer features, reducing diffusion model inference cost.
ai.why: Developers can adopt the technique to speed up image/video generation pipelines.

title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
excerpt: Spatial reasoning asks a model to work out where objects are in 3D space, how they relate to one another, and how they move. Agentic VLMs have recently brought large improvements on such tasks by letting the model actively gather evidence with 3D perception tools instead of answering in a single pass. Even so, on many questions the tools return the right evidence and the model still does not arrive at the correct answer: the gap between model and tools, where raw readings become usable conclusions, is left unfilled. We present S-Agent 2.0, a spatial reasoning agent that equips an off-the-shelf general coding agent with a command-line perception toolkit, and we design the interface around…

ai.summary: S‑Agent 2.0 is a general coding agent that actively uses 3D perception tools to gather evidence and perform spatial reasoning, closing the gap between tool outputs and correct answers on 3D tasks.
ai.why: Demonstrates how agentic VLMs can be made more reliable for geometry‑heavy applications, useful for building AI assistants that understand physical space.

title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
excerpt: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model…

ai.summary: CoEvo‑RSI introduces a framework that co‑evolves an AI model (brain) and its execution harness (body) to address the brain‑body mismatch problem in recursive self‑improving agents.
ai.why: Offers a systematic approach for building self‑improving AI systems where model capabilities stay aligned with evolving toolsets.

title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
excerpt: Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene. To this end, we introduce Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. We extend a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing that integrates complementary observations across cameras, and add a trajectory head that predicts how physical points move through time. Each trajectory tracks a single point across all views, and supervising these trajectories alongside video generation…

ai.summary: The Video‑Point Model (VPM) extends a pretrained world model with camera‑conditioned multi‑view processing to forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and predict 3D point trajectories given multi‑view video histories and language instructions.
ai.why: Enables developers to generate consistent multi‑view video predictions and plan in 4D environments, opening new possibilities for simulation and robotics.

title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
excerpt: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by…

ai.summary: The paper adds a correction step to diffusion sampling that adjusts intermediate predictions to reduce exposure‑bias error accumulation, improving sample quality without extra guidance.
ai.why: Allows developers to get cleaner diffusion outputs with minimal additional computation.

title: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
excerpt: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents increasingly act over streaming omni-modal observations spanning screenshots, audio, video, interaction history, and device states. However, exposing this complete context uniformly at every step ignores that relevance is transient and sparse: the signal determining one action can become clutter at the next. Because executed actions feed back into the context, these errors compound into Sequential Distraction, driving the agent into irreversible trajectory drift. We formulate the underlying requirement as Focused Perception: a representation that is step-adaptive, action-sufficient, and non-intrusive. We realize this in FocusGUI, a lightweight adapter…

ai.summary: The paper proposes a relevance‑focused architecture for GUI agents that selects the most pertinent omni‑modal observations at each step to avoid "Sequential Distraction" and improve action accuracy.
ai.why: Helps developers build more reliable agents that can operate over screenshots, audio, video and device state without being overwhelmed by irrelevant data.

title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
excerpt: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without…

ai.summary: SolarRenderer is a structure‑conditioned video renderer that turns coarse scene layouts, motion, and camera specs into realistic video in only a few denoising steps, independent of any specific game engine.
ai.why: Provides a fast, engine‑agnostic way to produce high‑quality video, useful for game developers and coding agents that need rapid visual feedback.

title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
excerpt: Moving from controllable videos to genuinely playable worlds requires persistent world state, executable game rules, and low-latency interaction. We outline a roadmap for the next generation of Matrix-Game that separates game execution from visual generation through an executable game harness, and introduce Matrix-Game 4.0 as the first system built on this design. A lightweight game engine maintains world state and executes interaction rules, a multimodal coding agent translates player ideas into game code and dynamic scene captions, and a renderer based on autoregressive video model transforms engine-rendered low-poly proxies into detailed visuals, conditioned on dynamic captions and…

ai.summary: Matrix-Game 4.0 separates game execution from visual generation by using a lightweight engine for world state and an executable harness, while a multimodal coding agent translates player ideas into game actions.

title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
excerpt: Looped language models can run more iterations at test time, but additional iterations need not help them solve longer problems. For sequential state tracking, final-answer supervision does not specify how far each iteration should advance, and repeated updates can change the scale of the recurrent state. We introduce Progress-Aligned Recurrence (PAR), which trains the prediction at iteration k to match the state after the first k operations and rescales recurrent states to their first-iteration norms. On swap-S_5, a Qwen2.5-0.5B model trained on at most 32 moves achieves 95.5\% mean full-state accuracy at 512 moves, or 16times the training length, compared with 55.7\% reported for RLT and…

ai.summary: Progress‑Aligned Recurrence (PAR) trains each iteration of a looped language model to predict the state after exactly k operations, enabling better length generalization in sequential state‑tracking tasks.
ai.why: Provides a concrete technique for extending language‑model reasoning to longer problems, useful for developers building stateful agents.

title: MMEnterprise-Bench: Evaluating Enterprise Agents over Evolving Multimodal Records
excerpt: Enterprise agents answer questions over workplace records that evolve through team collaboration. As information is shared, corrected, and revised across documents, chats, and figures, multiple versions of the same information accumulate in the workspace. Reliable question answering therefore requires agents to reason over sufficient evidence, resolve cross-source and temporal conflicts, and recognize when the available evidence is insufficient to establish an answer. To systematically evaluate these capabilities, we introduce MMEnterprise-Bench, a benchmark comprising 1,613 questions grounded in evolving multimodal records from simulated collaboration projects, covering three categories…

ai.summary: MMEnterprise-Bench is a benchmark that evaluates enterprise agents on evolving multimodal workplace records, testing their ability to reason over cross‑source, temporal conflicts and detect insufficient evidence.

title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
excerpt: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining…

ai.summary: Ropedia W0 is a foundation world model that learns egocentric locomotion and manipulation across humans and robots, trained on 10 k hours of human and 3 k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations.
ai.why: Provides a cross‑embodiment world model that can accelerate research on robots that need to both move and manipulate objects.

title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
excerpt: Decision models support routing, guardrails, and output verification in LLM systems. However, item accuracy alone cannot establish whether models make correct decisions across controlled variations or assign reliable confidence to their predictions. We introduce DecisionPivot, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 48 tasks and 40,033 items across seven decision roles. Its core track contains 7,800 items from 13 generated task families, organized into contrast groups with computed answers verified by independently implemented solvers. The complementary reference track contains 32,233 items from 35 public test sets, preserving their original evaluation metrics. We evaluate 40 decision models and…

ai.summary: DecisionPivot is a diagnostic benchmark containing 48 tasks and 40,033 items designed to evaluate the reliability and confidence calibration of decision models used for routing and guardrails in LLM systems.

title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
excerpt: In this report, we introduce Sage-A1.5, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that builds on A1 to advance long-horizon problem solving through adaptive capability composition. Compared with A1, Sage-A1.5 learns not only to solve individual tasks, but also to organize work and revise its approach during execution. Sage-A1.5 highlights three improvements: agentic orchestration, verification, and open scientific discovery. First, agentic orchestration extends single-agent execution through task delegation and parallel collaboration among subagents with isolated contexts, enabling complex tasks to be decomposed and addressed concurrently and supporting efficient execution while reducing…

ai.summary: Sage‑A1.5 is a 35‑billion‑parameter Mixture‑of‑Experts agentic model that adds adaptive capability composition, verification, and open scientific discovery to improve long‑horizon problem solving over its predecessor A1.
ai.why: Offers a powerful open‑weight model for developers needing autonomous multi‑step planning and verification in complex domains.

title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
excerpt: 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts. We present LLM2R, which casts part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM): a Point-BERT encoder and a Q-Former compress each part into a block of geometric tokens, the blocks of all parts are concatenated, and a causal LLM adapted with…

ai.summary: LLM2R proposes casting 3D part assembly as a sequence modeling task using a pretrained decoder LLM to predict SE(3) transformations for each part.
ai.why: The method offers a scalable way to assemble complex objects, opening new possibilities for AI‑driven CAD and robotics pipelines.

title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
excerpt: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together. We introduce Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs), which use a single denoiser to propose parallel revisions and evaluate a candidate draft. We train the denoiser to reconstruct every token from uniformly corrupted drafts, teaching both preservation and repair. Its predictions specify revisions directly, without a diffusion reverse transition. Evaluation requires a different use of these predictions: confidence in an existing token reflects both contextual support…

ai.summary: Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs) train a single denoiser to reconstruct tokens from uniformly corrupted drafts, allowing parallel token revisions and improving answer coherence.
ai.why: Offers a new technique for building more efficient reasoning LLMs that can refine outputs in parallel, potentially speeding up inference.

title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
excerpt: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. Under this receding-horizon paradigm, the unexecuted remainder---the action tail---is discarded, and the next chunk is regenerated from fresh noise. We show that this discarded tail retains transferable denoising progress: action-tail initialization can match or outperform a native 10-step Gaussian baseline using fewer denoising steps. However, the optimal denoising budget varies substantially across samples, indicating that tail reuse should be adapted to the updated environment. Based on…

ai.summary: VLA‑Rolling reuses the discarded denoising tail from previous action chunks as initialization for the next chunk, achieving comparable or better performance with fewer denoising steps.
ai.why: Reduces compute for vision‑language‑action models while preserving control, making real‑time planning more feasible.

title: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation
excerpt: Training high-quality diffusion models is computationally expensive, and inference-time guidance often adds further sampling cost. In this work, we introduce Swift, a simple yet effective self-guided training method that uses a frozen weak denoiser to improve a stronger model without adding inference overhead. For each noisy input, Swift extrapolates the clean regression target away from the weak denoiser's prediction, amplifying components that remain underfit. The weak guide can be an early training checkpoint, requires no backpropagation during main-model training, and is discarded afterward. The resulting model retains the original sampler and supports both conditional and unconditional…

ai.summary: Swift is a self‑guided training technique that uses a frozen weak denoiser to extrapolate target predictions for a stronger diffusion model, boosting quality without adding inference overhead.
ai.why: Provides a cheap way to enhance diffusion models, useful for developers seeking higher fidelity without slower inference.

title: PhysSkin++: Real-Time and Generalizable Physics-Based Animation via Self-Supervised Neural Skinning
excerpt: Generalizing real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and spatial discretizations remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce PhysSkin++, a physics-informed framework that learns continuous neural skinning fields from static geometries to construct compact deformation subspaces. Specifically, we propose a Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder that predicts shape-dependent deformation subspaces without per-object network training. To learn these subspaces without simulation trajectories, we develop a Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning strategy that combines skinning-field normalization with conflict-aware gradient correction, stabilizing joint optimization under…

ai.summary: PhysSkin++ introduces a neural skinning fields autoencoder that learns continuous deformation subspaces from static 3D geometries, enabling real‑time physics‑based animation without per‑object training.
ai.why: Developers can integrate fast, generalizable animation into games or simulations without costly simulation pipelines.

title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
excerpt: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate…

ai.summary: The paper introduces a model that simultaneously generates video and corresponding 3D motion for any supplied rig, outputting a camera trajectory that aligns the motion with the 3D scene.
ai.why: Enables developers to create replayable 3D animations directly from video generation models, opening new workflows for games and simulation.
